questions.q: In which year did Barry Allen first appear as the Flash, in Showcase #4?
questions.why: Barry debuted in Showcase #4, cover-dated October 1956, helping to kick off the Silver Age of comics.

questions.q: Barry Allen's debut was created by writer Robert Kanigher, artist Carmine Infantino and which editor?
questions.why: Editor Julius 'Julie' Schwartz led the team that reinvented the Flash in Showcase #4.

questions.q: What is Barry Allen's day job in the comics?
questions.why: Barry works as a forensic chemist, and a lightning strike in his lab, mixing with chemicals, gives him his speed.

questions.q: Where does Barry traditionally store his compressed Flash costume when not in use?
questions.why: A ring designed by Barry's father-in-law holds the compressed suit and can eject it when Barry needs to change.

questions.q: Who is Barry Allen's wife in the comics?
questions.why: Barry is engaged to, and later marries, Iris West, a reporter who is a parallel to Lois Lane.

questions.q: What DC concept did the 1961 story 'Flash of Two Worlds' introduce when Barry met Jay Garrick?
questions.why: Flash #123 revealed that Jay Garrick lived on a parallel Earth, establishing DC's Multiverse.

questions.q: Which secret ape civilisation first appeared in Barry Allen's classic stories?
questions.why: Barry's early stories added colorful sci-fi concepts including Gorilla City alongside his Rogues Gallery of villains.

questions.q: After Barry died in Crisis on Infinite Earths #8, how many years passed before his comic return?
questions.why: Barry sacrificed himself in 1985 and stayed dead for 23 years until he returned in 2008 and 2009.

questions.q: Who played Barry Allen in the CW television series The Flash?
questions.why: Grant Gustin played Barry in the Arrowverse, while Ezra Miller played him in the DC Extended Universe films.

questions.q: Which university professor, adoptive father of Barry's wife, designed Barry's costume and its compact storage?
questions.why: Professor Ira West built the Flash's suit and the ring, which keeps the costume compressed.
